title: Perfect quotient coefficient exchange with augmentation and completion-unit normalization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $u^*\dashv P=Ru_*$ for the canonical derived adjunction, with counit $\varepsilon$ and ordinary derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Use the completion reflector $C_T$ with unit $\eta_T$ and the full derived-complete subcategory of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]; thus $C_TV=R\lim_n(V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T)$ and $u_c^*=C_{\mathcal X}u^*\dashv P$ on complete objects. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use the small diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Their constant ring sheaves are $\Delta\underline A_T$ and their quotient ring sheaves are $B_T=(\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with the actual quotient transitions. A $B_T$-module system consists of module sheaves $M_n$ over $\underline{A_n}_T$ and $\underline{A_{n+1}}_T$-linear transition maps to $M_n$ by restriction of scalars. Write $U_T$ for restriction to constant-$A$ towers, $S_T=-\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$, $\mathcal R_T=S_T\Delta$, and $i_V:\Delta V\to U_T\mathcal R_TV$ for the quotient augmentation. Write $G=u^*$ termwise, $P^J=Ru_*^J$ for derived termwise direct image on constant-$A$ towers, $G_B\dashv P_B$ for the quotient-ring diagram adjunction, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on constant-$A$ towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. All derived adjunctions are the ones induced from the module adjunctions, not separately chosen hom-set bijections. Assume each $A_n$ is represented over $A$ by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules. For every $F\in D_{\mathcal X}$ let$$h_F:\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(PF)\longrightarrow P_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$$be the coefficient-exchange mate whose transpose, under $G_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}\cong\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}u^*$, is $S_{\mathcal X}\Delta(\varepsilon_F)$. Let $\chi_F:\Delta PF\xrightarrow{\sim}P^J\Delta F$ be the constant-tower comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization], and let $h^A_F:U_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}(PF)\to P^JU_{\mathcal X}\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$ be the strict-tower projection mate of [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate] for $u$, the object $F$ and the algebra tower $(\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y})_n$, with source identified through $\chi_F$. Under the canonical derived-composition comparison $d:U_{\mathcal Y}P_B\cong P^JU_{\mathcal X}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] one has $d\,U_{\mathcal Y}(h_F)=h^A_F$. The quotient-linear evaluation of $h_F$ at $n$ is a map$$h_{F,n}:(PF)\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y}\longrightarrow Ru_{*,A_n}(F\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal X})$$whose restriction to $A$ is the $n$-th evaluation of $h^A_F$, the ordinary counit-defined projection for the constant perfect coefficient $\underline{A_n}$. The maps $h_F$ and $h_{F,n}$ are natural isomorphisms. With the direct-image/limit comparison $a$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] and the identifications $\mathcal L_TU_T\mathcal R_T=C_T$ of [lem-pur-strict-quotient-diagonal-normalization], define$$\rho_F=a_{U_{\mathcal X}\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F}^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(h^A_F):C_{\mathcal Y}PF\longrightarrow PC_{\mathcal X}F.$$Then $\rho_F\eta_{\mathcal Y,PF}=P(\eta_{\mathcal X,F})$. All transitions in these identities are actual coefficient restrictions. No finite-cardinality assumption on $A_n$, flatness of $A\to A_n$, scheme hypothesis, or completeness of $F$ is imposed.

proof.text:
On the diagram sites use [lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward] to obtain the specified comparison $d:U_{\mathcal Y}P_B\cong P^JU_{\mathcal X}$. Here $u^{-1}B_{\mathcal Y}=B_{\mathcal X}$: [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] identifies inverse images of the constant quotient modules naturally in their quotient transitions, and the quotient maps defining the two diagrams are the same ring maps. The scalar-unit comparison $b:G U_{\mathcal Y}\to U_{\mathcal X}G_B$ is therefore an isomorphism. On flat-term K-flat representatives its map is $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, with inverse $r\otimes x\mapsto rx$; these are the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-restriction-counit] on these small diagram sites, with constant ring $A$ and algebra sheaves $B_T$. Its comparison is precisely $d$, since both use the same derived-composition normalization. It gives
$$U_{\mathcal X}(\varepsilon^B_N)b_{P_BN}=\varepsilon^J_{U_{\mathcal X}N}G(d_N).$$
Consequently, for any $t:M\to P_BN$ with transpose $t^\flat$, the transpose of $d_NU_{\mathcal Y}(t)$ is $U_{\mathcal X}(t^\flat)b_M$: substitute $G U(t)$ in this displayed equation, move it past $b$ by naturality, and use $\varepsilon^B_NG_B(t)=t^\flat$. This is an equality of the specified adjunction maps.

Apply Step 1 to $M=\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}PF$, $N=\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$ and $t=h_F$. Its transpose is the scalar extension of $\Delta\varepsilon_F$, preceded by the pullback/scalar-extension comparison. After forgetting coefficients and using $b$, this becomes
$$G U_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}PF\cong\Delta u^*PF\otimes^L B_{\mathcal X}\xrightarrow{\Delta\varepsilon_F\otimes1}\Delta F\otimes^LB_{\mathcal X}.$$
The tensor comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The constant-tower comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization] satisfies $\varepsilon^J_{\Delta F}G(\chi_F)=\Delta\varepsilon_F$. Thus the transpose of the strict-tower projection mate $h^A_F$, with its source identified by $\chi_F$, is exactly the same displayed arrow, as specified in the equivalent-transpose clause of [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate]. The adjunction bijection is injective, so $d\,U_{\mathcal Y}(h_F)=h^A_F$ before evaluation or inverse limit. No conservativity or faithfulness of evaluation is used to prove this equality.

source.place: Equation 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), Tags 07A4 and 07A6; compare the two counit transposes on the diagram site

proof.text: The evaluation-adjunction normalization in [lem-pur-quotient-diagram-projection-evaluation] carries the quotient-diagram adjunction, including its counit, to the specified $A_n$-coefficient adjunction. It therefore sends $h_F$ to the $A_n$-linear mate $h_{F,n}$ of the scalar extension of $\varepsilon_F$. Its source and target are $(PF)\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y}$ and $Ru_{*,A_n}(F\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal X})$. For example the cited evaluation statement can be applied with $H=F$, $K=\underline A_{\mathcal Y}$: both quotient projection maps with tensor-unit argument are identities by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], so its arrow $v$ is $h_F$. Apply the counit identity of [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-restriction-counit] also on the original sites with algebra sheaves $\underline{A_n}_T$, whose structural map $u^{-1}\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y}\cong\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal X}$ is the constant-module identification of [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]. The calculation in Step 1 then says that restriction to $A$ of $h_{F,n}$ is the adjunct of $u^*PF\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal X}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_F\otimes1}F\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal X}$. This is the ordinary counit-defined projection. The evaluation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate] identifies evaluation of $h^A_F$ with this same map. The quotient-diagram evaluation comparisons are natural and compatible with the actual quotient transitions by the cited evaluation lemma.

source.place: Equation 0B56 and Tag 07A6; quotient-diagram evaluation and coefficient-restriction normalization

proof.text: For each $n$ choose the bounded finite-projective $A$-complex $E_n^\bullet$ representing $A_n$, as in the hypothesis. A term $E_n^q$ is generated by finitely many elements, giving a surjection $A^r\to E_n^q$ by [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; lift its identity along that surjection using [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to obtain maps $E_n^q\to A^r\to E_n^q$ with composite identity. Apply the exact constant realization of [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] termwise to the representative isomorphism $E_n^\bullet\simeq A_n$ and to these splittings. The construction in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] identifies the resulting finite free sheaves with $\underline A_{\mathcal Y}^{\oplus r}$ and retains the splitting equations. Thus $\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y}$ is represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free coefficient sheaves, hence is perfect in exactly the sense required for the ringed-site projection formula. This argument is performed separately for each $n$; it does not require a uniform bound on their representatives or flatness of $A_n$ over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0944 (lemma-projection-formula), perfectness hypothesis; exact constant realization and finite-projective coefficient packages

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-ringed-site-perfect-projection-formula] to $u$, the arbitrary unbounded object $F$, and the perfect coefficient $\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal Y}$ from Step 4. Its canonical pullback is $\underline{A_n}_{\mathcal X}$ by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]. By Step 3, every evaluation of $h^A_F$ is therefore an isomorphism. To conclude for the strict tower, use [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]: evaluations are exact and a tower morphism is invertible when every component is. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], evaluation of each cohomology morphism $H^q(h^A_F)$ is $H^q$ of the corresponding evaluated arrow, hence invertible. Each $H^q(h^A_F)$ is thus invertible, and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] gives that $h^A_F$ is invertible in the derived category of strict towers. Step 2 and the isomorphism $d$ show that $U_{\mathcal Y}(h_F)$ is invertible. The exact conservative restriction of [lem-pur-strict-quotient-diagonal-normalization] (1) now gives that $h_F$ is invertible. Exact quotient evaluation is a functor on derived categories, so it sends its inverse to an inverse of every $h_{F,n}$. Naturality follows from the functorial adjunction transposes and the cited natural comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0944 (lemma-projection-formula); levelwise exactness of strict towers and the cohomological criterion for isomorphisms in the unbounded derived category

proof.text:
For the algebra tower $Q_{T,\bullet}=(\underline{A_n}_T)_n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate]. Its reduction functor $B_T$ is $U_T\mathcal R_T$, and its unit is the quotient augmentation $i$. Its strict derived-tower equality gives
$$h^A_F i_{\mathcal Y,PF}=P^J(i_{\mathcal X,F})\chi_F.$$
The identity is on the single strict coefficient diagram, and consequently uses its actual quotient restriction maps. It holds for arbitrary $F$, prior to taking limits.

Put $Q=U_{\mathcal X}\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}F$ and write $\ell_{T,V}:\mathcal L_T\Delta V\cong V$. By [lem-pur-strict-quotient-diagonal-normalization], $\eta_{T,V}=\mathcal L_T(i_V)\ell_{T,V}^{-1}$ and $\mathcal L_TU_T\mathcal R_T=C_T$, naturally. Apply $\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}$ to Step 6 and use naturality of $a$ in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. The definition of $\rho_F$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho_F\eta_{\mathcal Y,PF}
&=a_Q^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(h^A_Fi_{\mathcal Y,PF})\ell_{\mathcal Y,PF}^{-1}\\
&=P(\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}i_{\mathcal X,F})\,a_{\Delta F}^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(\chi_F)\ell_{\mathcal Y,PF}^{-1}\\
&=P(\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}i_{\mathcal X,F})P(\ell_{\mathcal X,F}^{-1})=P(\eta_{\mathcal X,F}).
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate equality is exactly the constant-tower limit normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization], rearranged as $a_{\Delta F}^{-1}\mathcal L_{\mathcal Y}(\chi_F)\ell_{\mathcal Y,PF}^{-1}=P(\ell_{\mathcal X,F}^{-1})$. Thus the required completion-unit equation concerns the specified $a$, $d$ and augmentations. All comparisons used above are natural. Only the perfectness assumption was used for invertibility; none of the steps imposes finite cardinality, flat quotient maps, a scheme presentation, or completeness of $F$.

lean.statement: theorem perfectQuotientExchangeNormalization [IsNoetherianRing A] (hperfect : PerfectQuotients A I) : ∃ (p : Presentation f A I) (d : p.push.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ p.atY.restrictionD ≅ p.atX.restrictionD ⋙ f.towerPush A), PresentationNormalized f A I p ∧ d.hom = restrictionMate p ∧ (∀ F : X.derived A, p.atY.restrictionD.map ((exchange p).app F) ≫ d.hom.app (p.atX.reductionD.obj F) = (strictExchange p).app F) ∧ (∀ (F : X.derived A) (n : ℕ), (finiteExchange p n).app F = f.finiteProjection A I n F) ∧ (∀ (F : X.derived A) (n : ℕ), (Y.evaluate A n).map ((strictExchange p).app F) ≫ (Y.evaluate A n).map ((f.towerPush A).map (p.reductionX.tower.hom.app F)) ≫ (f.evaluatePushIso A n).hom.app ((X.reduction A I).obj F) ≫ (f.push A).map ((X.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app F) ≫ (f.finiteRestrictionPushIso A I n).hom.app ((X.finiteReduction A I n).obj F) = (Y.evaluate A n).map (p.reductionY.tower.hom.app ((f.push A).obj F)) ≫ (Y.finiteEvaluationIso A I n).hom.app ((f.push A).obj F) ≫ (Y.finiteRestriction A I n).map ((finiteExchange p n).app F)) ∧ IsIso (exchange p) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (finiteExchange p n)) ∧ (∀ F : X.derived A, (Y.unit A I).app ((f.push A).obj F) ≫ completionExchange p F = (f.push A).map ((X.unit A I).app F))
